title: Physical books scanned to train AI, then recycled; rare volumes #AItraining #copyright #books
description:
The narrative centers on how Anthropic, an AI company, sourced training data by acquiring and scanning millions of physical books, including antique editions, to improve the AI’s understanding of human language. This approach follows a costly legal setback involving the unauthorized use of pirated books, which resulted in significant fines. To avoid further copyright infringement, Anthropic shifted to physically purchasing books, cutting them open to scan every page, then recycling the originals, effectively destroying the physical copies. This method ensures ownership rights over the content since buying a physical book grants ownership, unlike e-books, which typically provide only a license to read. The strategy highlights the importance of high-quality, human-written material—especially carefully researched and edited texts—to enhance AI pre-training. The story contrasts Anthropic’s approach with others in the AI industry who preserve rare books, demonstrating different ethical and legal handling of training data. The business value lies in securing exclusive, legally compliant data sources, which directly elevate AI performance and reliability while navigating complex copyright constraints. #AItraining #MachineLearning #ArtificialIntelligence
